arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Neal Katyal argued the cross should not be destroyed. He cited four facts about the memorial. He emphasized the historical context of the monument.
David Carvin argued the cross fits a sensible Establishment Clause analysis. He suggested using the Town of Greece coercion test. He claimed this approach protects religious liberty.
General Wall argued the cross is permissible under Town of Greece. He cited the nation's tradition of accommodating religious speech. He argued this resolves the case easily.
Ms. Miller argued the Establishment Clause prohibits preferring one religion. She focused on the core constitutional principle. She distinguished between endorsement and accommodation.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The American Legion and the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission defend the Peace Cross. They argue the symbol honors fallen soldiers and fits within a long civic tradition. The American Humanist Association opposes the memorial. They argue the government cannot display a religious symbol in a public park.
